chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the divorce by which she is not permitted [to marry her first husband] 'until she marries another husband.' He said, 'I will inform you of what I did with a woman who was with me, and I wanted to divorce her, so I left her until she menstruated and purified herself, then I divorced her without sexual intercourse and testified over that with two witnesses. Then I left her until the waiting period was about to expire, so I returned her and had intercourse with her, and I left her until she menstruated and purified herself, then I divorced her while pure without sexual intercourse with two witnesses. Then I left her until before the waiting period expired, so I returned her and had intercourse with her until she menstruated and purified herself, then I divorced her while pure without sexual intercourse with witnesses. And I did that with her because I had no need of her.'

As for the return (re-marriage without a new contract), it is necessary for whoever wants the divorce of the waiting period, and testifying over the return is recommended and desirable, but that is not a condition of it. That is indicated by what was narrated:

key_terms.حَتَّى تَنْكِحَ زَوْجاً غَيْرَهُ: Until she marries another husband (condition for re-permission)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct procedure for a husband to divorce his wife conditionally so she becomes permissible to him again after marrying another?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the mechanics of *Talaq al-Mu'allaq* by demonstrating a three-cycle ritual of divorce and return (*raj'a*) with a woman, ensuring each separation occurs during a period of purity (*tuhr*) without intercourse and with two witnesses. This practical example underscores the Shia jurisprudential distinction that while witnessing the return is recommended (*mandub*), it is not a strict condition for the validity of the divorce, allowing the husband to retain the right to remarry her directly after the third cycle.
